clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old male presented with a 6-year history of progressive cerebellar syndrome (imbalance, diplopia, slurred speech evolving to inability to walk, dysphagia, and dysarthria) and a concurrent 2-year history of a partially ulcerated erythematous scapular skin plaque. Diagnostic workup revealed histopathological confirmation of LCH on skin biopsy, demonstrating histiocytic proliferation with eosinophils and atypical mitotic figures (E002) with positive immunohistochemistry for CD1a, S100, and langerin (E003). The patient failed pulse methylprednisolone therapy and subsequently developed diabetes insipidus (E004), confirming progressive hypothalamic-pituitary involvement characteristic of multisystem LCH. These findings established LCH as the unifying diagnosis explaining the progressive neurological deterioration.
